summary.title: Secure Mobile-Money Payments API
summary.description: CSSS 441 Project 1, Week 1: level-1 DFD, STRIDE-per-element threats, risk ratings and top-five controls.

diagrams.title: Level-1 DFD: Mobile-Money Payments API
diagrams.description: Level-1 data-flow diagram of the secure mobile-money payments API: 4 external entities, 6 processes, 5 data stores, 19 flows and 5 trust boundaries.

data.name: Internet (untrusted)
data.description: Everything outside our control: customer and agent devices, merchant systems and the third-party SMS/email provider.

data.name: Admin network (allow-listed)
data.description: Network ranges allowed to reach the admin console. Membership is enforced by firewall rules, not by client-supplied headers.

data.name: Application zone (Docker network)
data.description: API, auth, ledger, webhook, audit and admin services on the private Docker Compose network. Target design: only the edge port is published.

data.name: Data zone (PostgreSQL, Redis)
data.description: Databases and cache. Reachable only from the application zone with per-service credentials over TLS.

data.name: Secrets zone (Vault)
data.description: HashiCorp Vault (or environment secrets in the lab). Reachable only with a service identity.

data.name: Wallet User (customer / agent)
data.description: Customer or cash-in/out agent using the wallet API from a mobile or web client.

threats.title: T26 Wallet user denies initiating a transfer
threats.description: A customer disputes a transfer, and the system cannot show who authorised it from which session. Rating: L3 x I3 = 9 (Medium). Reason: Disputes are routine in mobile money, but a single disputed transfer has bounded impact.
threats.mitigation: Step-up authentication (TOTP or passkey) above a transfer threshold; audit entries tied to session and device; confirmation notification to the user.

data.name: Merchant
data.description: Merchant backend that calls the payments API and receives signed webhooks.

data.name: SMS / Email Provider
data.description: Third-party service that delivers recovery codes and reset links.

data.name: Administrator
data.description: Operations staff using the admin console from the allow-listed network, with MFA.

data.name: Admin Console
data.description: Web console for admins. MFA required; reachable only from the allow-listed network.

threats.title: T13 Admin account takeover or CSRF used to freeze wallets, change limits or reverse transactions
threats.description: Attacker hijacks an admin session or tricks an admin browser into issuing privileged requests. Rating: L2 x I5 = 10 (Medium). Reason: MFA and the allow-list make takeover unlikely, but admin actions have the highest impact.
threats.mitigation: WebAuthn MFA; short sessions; step-up re-authentication for sensitive actions; CSRF tokens and SameSite=Strict; named admin accounts.

data.name: API Gateway and Authorization Layer
data.description: TLS termination, request-schema validation, session check, rate limiting, security headers and the deny-by-default role plus ownership authorization layer for every route.

threats.title: T27 Privilege escalation through client-controlled role or claims
threats.description: The server trusts a role, wallet owner or merchant ID supplied by the client instead of its own session record. Rating: L2 x I5 = 10 (Medium). Reason: Server-side sessions make this unlikely, but one trusted client field would give admin or merchant powers.
threats.mitigation: Derive role and identity only from the server-side session; ignore client-supplied role fields; authorization tests for every role against every route.

data.name: Webhook Dispatcher
data.description: Builds, signs (HMAC-SHA-256 plus timestamp) and delivers merchant webhooks with retries.

threats.title: T24 Slow or unreachable merchant endpoints and retry storms exhaust dispatcher workers
threats.description: Webhook delivery to slow or dead endpoints ties up workers and delays other merchants. Rating: L3 x I2 = 6 (Low). Reason: Failure is confined to webhook delivery; the ledger and API keep working.
threats.mitigation: Connect and read timeouts; bounded queue with exponential backoff and dead-letter; per-merchant circuit breaker.

data.name: Wallet and Ledger Service
data.description: Wallets, balances and transfers on a double-entry ledger, with database transactions, daily limits and idempotency keys.

threats.title: T07 Retried or concurrent requests cause double payment or overdraft
threats.description: TOP FIVE #4. A client retry, or parallel requests fired on purpose, pays twice or spends more than the balance. Rating: L4 x I4 = 16 (High). Reason: Mobile networks force client retries and an attacker can fire parallel requests; each success is direct financial loss.
threats.mitigation: Mandatory idempotency key with a unique constraint; database transactions with row locks (or serialisable isolation); daily limit and balance checked inside the same transaction.

threats.title: T08 Business-logic abuse: negative or zero amounts, rounding, currency mix-ups, self-transfers
threats.description: Crafted but schema-valid requests mint funds or reverse a transfer. Rating: L3 x I5 = 15 (High). Reason: The requests look valid to the schema layer, and a ledger-integrity failure would be severe.
threats.mitigation: Integer minor units; amount > 0 and CHECK constraints; double-entry invariant (entries sum to zero) enforced in the database; property-based tests.

data.name: Auth Service
data.description: Registration, login, account recovery, TOTP and passkey (WebAuthn) second factors, session issuance, per-account and per-IP throttling, Argon2id hashing.

threats.title: T01 Credential stuffing and password guessing against login
threats.description: TOP FIVE #3. Attacker replays leaked username/password pairs or guesses passwords to take over a wallet. Rating: L5 x I4 = 20 (High). Reason: Leaked-credential lists are cheap, login is internet-facing, and a taken-over wallet means direct loss of funds.
threats.mitigation: Argon2id hashing; per-account and per-IP throttling; TOTP or passkey second factor; reject breached and common passwords at registration and password change.

threats.title: T15 User enumeration through login, registration and recovery responses or timing
threats.description: Different messages or response times reveal which phone numbers or emails have accounts. Rating: L4 x I2 = 8 (Medium). Reason: Easy to automate, but the impact is limited to learning which accounts exist.
threats.mitigation: Identical generic responses; hash comparison runs even for unknown users; throttling on all three endpoints.

data.name: Audit Logger
data.description: Writes hash-chained audit entries and runs the verifier that detects edits.

threats.title: T21 Missing or unattributed audit events let a user or admin deny an action
threats.description: A dispute cannot be resolved because an event was never logged, or lacks actor, object or trustworthy time. Rating: L3 x I4 = 12 (Medium). Reason: Logging gaps are common, and disputes over transfers are routine in payment systems.
threats.mitigation: Log actor, action, object, request ID and NTP-synchronised timestamp for every authentication, transfer and admin event; test that each event type is written; keep secrets and personal data out of logs.

data.name: Session and Throttle Cache (Redis)
data.description: Server-side sessions, MFA state and throttle counters.

data.name: Accounts and Credentials DB (PostgreSQL)
data.description: Accounts, Argon2id password hashes, encrypted TOTP seeds, WebAuthn credentials, merchant API-key hashes.

data.name: Ledger DB (PostgreSQL)
data.description: Double-entry ledger entries, balances, idempotency keys and daily-limit counters.

data.name: Audit Log Store (hash-chained)
data.description: Append-only audit entries; each entry carries the hash of the previous one.

data.name: Secrets Vault
data.description: DB credentials, webhook signing secrets, session-signing and TOTP-encryption keys.

threats.title: T25 Vault outage stops key retrieval and halts payments
threats.description: Services cannot fetch keys or credentials and fail, or fail open. Rating: L2 x I3 = 6 (Low). Reason: Low likelihood in a single-node lab, and services can cache keys in memory.
threats.mitigation: Fetch keys at startup and cache in memory with a TTL; documented restart procedure; fail closed and alert.

data.name: Wallet API requests and responses
data.description: Wallet User (customer / agent) to API Gateway and Authorization Layer. Crosses a trust boundary.

threats.title: T02 Broken object-level authorization on wallet and transaction routes
threats.description: TOP FIVE #1. A logged-in user changes a wallet or transaction ID, or calls a merchant, agent or admin route, to read or move another account's funds. Rating: L4 x I5 = 20 (High). Reason: Most common API flaw, trivial to try with an intercepting proxy, and the result is direct theft and data exposure.
threats.mitigation: Deny-by-default authorization layer: role check plus ownership check on every wallet and transaction route, with one negative test per route in CI.

threats.title: T03 Tampered request fields and injection payloads
threats.description: TOP FIVE #5. Attacker alters amount, recipient, currency or IDs, adds unexpected fields (mass assignment), or sends SQL/script payloads and oversized bodies. Rating: L4 x I4 = 16 (High). Reason: Every endpoint takes attacker-controlled input from a public network, and one validation gap can change a transfer.
threats.mitigation: Strict request schemas that reject unknown fields (Pydantic/Zod); parameterised queries only; output encoding; Semgrep in CI.

threats.title: T04 Session tokens or financial data exposed in transit or through verbose errors
threats.description: Tokens or balances are read from network traffic, or leak through stack traces, headers, URLs or logs. Rating: L3 x I4 = 12 (Medium). Reason: TLS 1.3 makes passive interception hard; the realistic exposure is misconfiguration, stack traces and weak cookie flags.
threats.mitigation: TLS 1.3 with HSTS; Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite cookies; generic error messages; security headers; no tokens or personal data in URLs or logs.

threats.title: T05 Request flooding and expensive queries
threats.description: Attacker floods the API or triggers costly queries so legitimate users cannot transact. Rating: L4 x I3 = 12 (Medium). Reason: Costs the attacker nothing, but the impact is availability only, not loss of funds.
threats.mitigation: Per-IP and per-account rate limits at the edge; body-size limits; timeouts; pagination caps; container resource limits.

data.name: Merchant API requests and responses
data.description: Merchant to API Gateway and Authorization Layer. Crosses a trust boundary.

threats.title: T06 Stolen or leaked merchant API key
threats.description: A leaked key is used to create payments or refunds, or to read a merchant's transactions. Rating: L3 x I4 = 12 (Medium). Reason: Merchants commit keys to repositories or log them; scoping and revocation limit the blast radius, which keeps likelihood moderate.
threats.mitigation: Keys stored hashed; scoped per merchant; rotation and revocation; optional IP allow-list; alerts on unusual volume.

data.name: Signed webhook callbacks
data.description: Webhook Dispatcher to Merchant. Crosses a trust boundary.

threats.title: T09 Forged webhook claiming a payment succeeded
threats.description: Attacker posts a fake 'payment succeeded' callback to a merchant endpoint. Rating: L3 x I5 = 15 (High). Reason: Merchants release goods on webhooks, and a forger needs no access to our systems, only the merchant's URL.
threats.mitigation: HMAC-SHA-256 over timestamp plus body with a per-merchant secret; constant-time verification in the reference receiver.

threats.title: T10 Replay of a captured, validly signed webhook
threats.description: A genuine webhook is captured and sent again later to trigger a second fulfilment. Rating: L3 x I4 = 12 (Medium). Reason: Capturing a webhook needs a vantage point such as merchant logs or a proxy, but replaying it then needs no secret.
threats.mitigation: Signed timestamp with a 5-minute tolerance; unique event-ID deduplication at the receiver; TLS only.

threats.title: T11 SSRF through a merchant-supplied webhook URL
threats.description: A merchant registers a URL pointing at internal hosts or cloud metadata, so the dispatcher reaches and leaks internal data. Rating: L3 x I4 = 12 (Medium). Reason: Any registered merchant controls the URL, and impact depends on what the dispatcher can reach internally.
threats.mitigation: HTTPS only; resolve the host and block private, loopback and link-local ranges; no redirects; egress firewall for the dispatcher; never return response bodies to the merchant.

data.name: Admin console session
data.description: Administrator to Admin Console. Crosses a trust boundary.

threats.title: T12 Admin allow-list bypass via spoofed X-Forwarded-For or a foothold on the allow-listed network
threats.description: Attacker forges a client-IP header, or compromises a host inside the allowed range, to reach the admin console. Rating: L3 x I5 = 15 (High). Reason: Header-trust mistakes are common and easy to test, and admin access is total.
threats.mitigation: Enforce the allow-list at the network firewall and from the proxy's verified peer address, never from client-supplied headers; MFA still required; test with a spoofed header.

data.name: Admin operations via API
data.description: Admin Console to API Gateway and Authorization Layer. Stays inside one trust zone.

data.name: Register, login, recovery and MFA requests
data.description: API Gateway and Authorization Layer to Auth Service. Stays inside one trust zone.

labels: Register, login, recovery and MFA requests

data.name: Authorised wallet and transfer commands
data.description: API Gateway and Authorization Layer to Wallet and Ledger Service. Stays inside one trust zone.

data.name: Payment events for webhook dispatch
data.description: Wallet and Ledger Service to Webhook Dispatcher. Stays inside one trust zone.

data.name: Recovery code or reset link
data.description: Auth Service to SMS / Email Provider. Crosses a trust boundary.

threats.title: T14 Account takeover through the recovery channel
threats.description: TOP FIVE #2. Attacker uses SIM swap or an intercepted code, a guessable or reusable reset token, or a recovery flow that skips the second factor. Rating: L4 x I5 = 20 (High). Reason: Recovery is usually the weakest path into an account, and SMS delivery is a known target for SIM-swap fraud.
threats.mitigation: Random 128-bit single-use token stored hashed, 15-minute expiry; recovery never bypasses MFA (or triggers a cooling-off period and notification); throttled attempts; identical responses for known and unknown accounts.

data.name: Credential and profile reads and writes
data.description: Auth Service to Accounts and Credentials DB (PostgreSQL). Crosses a trust boundary.

threats.title: T16 Credential database dump exposes password hashes and TOTP seeds
threats.description: SQL injection, a stolen backup or an over-privileged role exposes credential data. Rating: L2 x I5 = 10 (Medium). Reason: Parameterised queries and network isolation lower the odds, but exposure enables offline cracking and MFA bypass.
threats.mitigation: Argon2id with benchmarked parameters; TOTP secrets encrypted with a key held in Vault, not in the database; least-privilege DB role; TLS to PostgreSQL; encrypted backups.

labels: Credential and profile reads and writes

data.name: Session, MFA state and throttle counters
data.description: Auth Service to Session and Throttle Cache (Redis). Crosses a trust boundary.

threats.title: T17 Session theft or fixation through an exposed Redis or a pre-set session ID
threats.description: Attacker reads sessions from an open Redis, or forces a known session ID onto a victim. Rating: L3 x I4 = 12 (Medium). Reason: Redis is unauthenticated by default and Compose files often publish its port.
threats.mitigation: Redis ACL and TLS with no published port; new session ID at login; high-entropy IDs stored hashed; short idle and absolute timeouts.

labels: Session, MFA state and throttle counters

data.name: Session validation and rate-limit counters
data.description: API Gateway and Authorization Layer to Session and Throttle Cache (Redis). Crosses a trust boundary.

threats.title: T18 Throttle counters flushed or unavailable, so rate limiting fails open
threats.description: Counters are deleted, evicted or unreachable and the API stops limiting login attempts. Rating: L2 x I4 = 8 (Medium). Reason: Needs a Redis fault or access, but fail-open is a common default.
threats.mitigation: Fail closed when the counter store is unreachable; no-eviction policy for counter keys; alert on Redis errors.

data.name: Ledger transactions and idempotency keys
data.description: Wallet and Ledger Service to Ledger DB (PostgreSQL). Crosses a trust boundary.

threats.title: T19 Direct modification of ledger rows by a compromised credential or insider
threats.description: Someone with the application's DB credential updates or deletes ledger entries to move or hide money. Rating: L2 x I5 = 10 (Medium). Reason: Needs a privileged credential, but the ledger is the system of record.
threats.mitigation: App DB role has INSERT-only on ledger entries; corrections as reversing entries; daily reconciliation (entries sum to zero, balances match entries); database audit logging.

data.name: Access-control decisions and admin actions
data.description: API Gateway and Authorization Layer to Audit Logger. Stays inside one trust zone.

data.name: Authentication events
data.description: Auth Service to Audit Logger. Stays inside one trust zone.

data.name: Financial events
data.description: Wallet and Ledger Service to Audit Logger. Stays inside one trust zone.

data.name: Hash-chained audit entries
data.description: Audit Logger to Audit Log Store (hash-chained). Crosses a trust boundary.

threats.title: T20 Audit entries edited or deleted to hide fraud
threats.description: Attacker with database write access alters or removes audit rows. Rating: L2 x I4 = 8 (Medium). Reason: Needs database write access; the hash chain makes edits detectable, but a full rewrite is only caught with an external anchor.
threats.mitigation: Hash chain plus scheduled verifier; append-only DB role; periodically export the head hash off-host.

data.name: Webhook signing secrets
data.description: Webhook Dispatcher to Secrets Vault. Crosses a trust boundary.

threats.title: T22 Webhook signing secrets leaked through env vars, logs, source or an over-broad Vault token
threats.description: Secrets that sign webhooks are exposed, letting an attacker forge valid callbacks for that merchant. Rating: L3 x I5 = 15 (High). Reason: A leaked secret forges valid webhooks, and configuration and logs leak secrets routinely.
threats.mitigation: Secrets from Vault using short-lived AppRole tokens; per-merchant secrets with rotation; gitleaks in CI; log redaction.

data.name: Session-signing and TOTP-encryption keys
data.description: Auth Service to Secrets Vault. Crosses a trust boundary.

threats.title: T23 Rogue service or stolen token obtains session-signing and TOTP-encryption keys
threats.description: An attacker with a foothold in the application network presents a stolen token to Vault. Rating: L2 x I5 = 10 (Medium). Reason: Needs a foothold inside the application network, but the keys protect every session and every TOTP seed.
threats.mitigation: Per-service Vault policies; short token TTL; Vault audit device; network policy so only the auth service can reach the key path.
